sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: Topological sort handles dependencies in a **directed acyclic graph** (DAG), producing an order in which every node comes [[primary|after all its prerequisites]].
items: Compute each node's **in-degree**: the number of edges pointing to it
Put nodes with in-degree 0 into a queue — they have no unfinished prerequisites
Dequeue a node into the result and remove its outgoing edges, **decrementing the in-degree** of successors
Nodes whose in-degree drops to 0 are enqueued; repeat until the queue is empty

sections.heading: Operation Complexity
sections.content: Each node is enqueued once and each edge is removed once.
items: **Time complexity**: [[success|O(V + E)]], where V is the number of nodes and E the number of edges
**Space complexity**: [[success|O(V)]] for the in-degree table and queue
This is **Kahn's algorithm**; the alternative is reversing the DFS post-order

sections.heading: Properties & Uses
sections.content: The result is not necessarily unique — when several nodes have in-degree 0, their order is interchangeable.
items: **Cycle detection**: if fewer than V nodes get processed, the graph has a [[danger|cycle]] and cannot be sorted
**Real uses**: course prerequisite planning, build-tool dependency order, task scheduling
**Limit**: only works on DAGs; a graph with a cycle has no valid topological order
